title: Introduction
text: Overview section introducing the FIRST Tech Challenge Competition Manual and its structure.

title: About FIRST
text: FIRST® (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology) was founded by inventor Dean Kamen to inspire young people’s interest in science and technology. FIRST is a youth-serving nonprofit advancing STEM education. Programs include FIRST Robotics Competition, FIRST Tech Challenge, and FIRST LEGO League.

title: FIRST Tech Challenge
text: FIRST Tech Challenge is a student-centered robotics program where teams design, build, test, and program robots to compete in annual game challenges released at Kickoff.

title: FIRST Ethos and Core Values
text: FIRST Core Values include Discovery, Innovation, Impact, Inclusion, Teamwork, and Fun, expressed through Gracious Professionalism and Coopertition.

title: Core Values
text: Core Values emphasize teamwork, respect, learning, and inclusion in all FIRST programs.

title: Gracious Professionalism
text: Gracious Professionalism encourages high quality work, respect for others, and meaningful contributions while treating everyone with dignity.

title: Coopertition
text: Coopertition means competing while also helping and learning from others when possible.

title: Spirit of Volunteering
text: FIRST relies on volunteers who contribute their time to support teams, events, and the overall mission of inspiring students.

title: Accessibility and Inclusion
text: FIRST is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for participants with disabilities when requested in advance.

title: Document Conventions
text: Explains how the Competition Manual is structured, interpreted, and formatted, including rule numbering and definitions.

title: Translations & Versions
text: The manual is originally written in English and may be translated, but the English version is authoritative.

title: Team Updates
text: Team Updates communicate official changes and clarifications to the season documentation.

title: Question and Answer System
text: The Q&A system allows teams to ask rule questions and receive official clarifications during the season.

title: FIRST Season Overview
text: FIRST is the sport where every kid can go pro. As the world’s leading nonprofit that prepares young people for the future, FIRST offers robotics programs that build skills, confidence, and resilience. The 2025–2026 season, FIRST AGE presented by Qualcomm, is inspired by archaeology and discovery. Teams work collaboratively to solve themed robotics challenges and uncover new innovations.

title: Competition Eligibility and Inspection
text: This section defines eligibility requirements for teams, event check-in rules, awards eligibility, and match participation requirements including robot inspection rules and compliance with FIRST Tech Challenge regulations.

title: Team Eligibility Rules
text: Teams must be registered with FIRST and meet competition-ready requirements including registration, fees, youth protection screening, and roster completion. Requirements vary by region.

title: Team Registration Requirement
text: Teams must be registered with FIRST and complete all required registration, fees, and youth protection requirements to compete.

title: Event Check-in Requirement
text: Teams must check in on time with required documentation, roster information, and a student present.

title: Adult Supervision Requirement
text: At least one responsible adult must be present for the entire event and must follow FIRST Code of Conduct expectations.

title: Match Eligibility Rules
text: Teams must pass robot inspection before competing in matches. Inspectors have final authority on robot legality, and robots may be re-inspected at any time.

title: Robot Ownership Requirement
text: The robot and its major mechanisms must be built by the registered team, though outside assistance is allowed in limited forms such as fabrication or advice.

title: Single Robot Rule
text: Each team may only compete with one robot per event and may not switch between multiple robots during competition.

title: Inspection Requirement
text: Teams must pass initial robot inspection before participating in qualification or playoff matches.

title: Robot Presentation for Inspection
text: Teams must present their full robot, including all mechanisms and electronics, during inspection.

title: Re-Inspection Rules
text: Changes to a robot after inspection may require re-inspection unless they fall under defined exceptions such as fasteners, labeling, code updates, or identical replacements.

title: Re-Inspection Abuse
text: Teams may not exploit re-inspection rules to bypass other competition requirements.

title: Robot Power During Inspection
text: Robots may be powered on during inspection if necessary for evaluation.

title: Student Presence Requirement
text: At least one student must be present during robot inspection.

title: Advancement
text: Teams are only eligible to advance from events within their home region. Teams may be invited to compete at tournaments outside of their home region for additional gameplay, but are not advancement eligible from those events. Teams are assigned to regions through FTC-Events and may request reassignment through FIRST if geographically isolated or lacking a Program Delivery Partner. Teams advance through Qualifying Tournaments (QT) and League Tournaments (LT), with limits on advancement eligibility based on participation rules.

title: Advancement Points Calculation
text: Teams are ranked at each event based on advancement points earned through Qualification Performance, Alliance Lead selection, Draft Order Acceptance, Playoff Performance, and Judged Awards. Top ranked teams not yet advanced fill available advancement slots.

title: Qualification Phase Performance
text: Qualification Phase Performance points are calculated using an inverse error function based on team rank R, number of teams N, and alpha value 1.07. The result produces a near-normal distribution of points, with higher ranked teams receiving more points, typically ranging from 16 for top rank to lower values for lower ranks.

title: Alliance Selection Results
text: Alliance selection points reflect both qualification ranking and peer selection. Alliance leads earn points based on selection order, and selected partners receive equivalent points. The system rewards both strong qualification performance and strategic value to alliances.

title: Playoff Performance
text: Teams earn playoff advancement points based on final alliance placement. First place earns 40 points, second place 20 points, third place 10 points, and fourth place 5 points. All alliance members receive equal points.

title: Team Judged Awards
text: Judged awards contribute advancement points. Inspire Award earns 60 points for first place, 30 for second, and 15 for third. Other first place awards earn 12 points, second place 6 points, and third place 3 points. Awards not judged at the event or not team-based do not earn points.

title: Advancement Distribution by Region
text: Advancement distribution is determined by Program Delivery Partners and published before events. FIRST Headquarters allocates advancement slots for championship and premier events based on registration numbers, regional participation, and global representation. Unused advancement slots may be reallocated.

title: *Personal safety comes first
text:
*Personal safety comes first. All team members must observe the following safety practices throughout the event:

A.      wear safety glasses or safety rated glasses with side shields (ANSI-approved, UL Listed, CE EN166 rated, AS/NZS certified, or CSA rated) while in and around the playing FIELD and in the pit area. Clear or lightly tinted safety glasses are preferred. Shaded glasses are allowed for those who need them and do not require a specific accommodation request. The only instances where teams are not required to wear safety glasses are in their first 10 minutes of their event load in, and for the first 10 minutes pits are open each day of the event as long as they’re not working on the ROBOT or setting up their pit,

B.      wear closed toed/heeled shoes,

C.      control entanglement risks by tying back long hair and removing other dangling decorations including lanyards, spirit wear and rings as needed while working on or around a ROBOT or ROBOT related materials or tools,

D.      wear appropriate clothing,

E.      walk in the venue, and

F.      comply with government and venue-specific health and safety requirements in place for that event (i.e., mask wearing).

Teams are responsible for bringing their own personal protective equipment.

For more information about safety at FIRST events, please reference the FIRST Safety Manual.

A partial list of footwear that is not allowed: Crocs, slides, sandals, flip flops, Birkenstocks, sandals with an ankle strap, clogs.

title: *Be Nice
text:
*Be Nice. All participants should strive to be gracious and professional at all times while attending a FIRST Tech Challenge event. Uncivil behavior toward any participants is not tolerated.

Examples of inappropriate behavior include, but are not limited to:

A.      use of offensive language or other uncivil conduct towards someone,

B.      “weaponizing Gracious Professionalism” by accusing another person or team of being “not GP”,

C.      intentionally blocking the view of other participants or spectators for an extended period (Team members momentarily holding up team signs while directly supporting their team is not considered a violation of this rule.), and

D.      jamming or interfering with the remote sensing capabilities of a ROBOT or the FIELD while in open-access spectator seating areas.

Examples of remote sensing capabilities include, but are not limited to, vision systems, acoustic range finders, sonars, and infrared proximity sensors.

Use of imagery that, to a reasonably astute observer, mimics the AprilTags employed on the FIELD is a violation of this rule.

Examples of particularly contemptible behavior that may result in ejection from the event include, but are not limited to, the following:

E.      assault, e.g., throwing something that hits another person (even if unintended),

F.      threat, e.g., saying something like “if you don’t reverse that call, I’ll make you regret it,”

G.     harassment, e.g., badgering someone with no new information after a decision has been made or a question has been answered,

H.     bullying, e.g., using body or verbal language to cause another person to feel inadequate or unsafe,

I.        insulting, e.g., telling someone they do not deserve to be on a team,

J.      swearing at another person (versus swearing under one’s breath or at oneself), and

K.      yelling at another person(s) in anger or frustration.

title: *Children with adults, please
text: *Children with adults, please. Children under 12 must be accompanied in the pits by an adult at all times.

title: *Respect the venue
text: *Respect the venue. Teams may not damage the venue, including but not limited to bleachers, floors, walls, railings, in any way. This includes littering with team giveaways including candies, flyers, and stickers.

title: *Teams must check in
text:
*Teams must check in. An adult team member must check in at the Pit Administration station, or the designated check in location, no later than 45 minutes before Qualification MATCHES are scheduled to start unless otherwise specified or approved by the Event Director.

Violation: Failure to check in may result in a team not participating in the event.

title: *Event resources are for competing teams only
displayTitle: E106 Event resources are for competing teams only
text: *Event resources are for competing teams only. Only teams registered for an event may use that event’s competition FIELD, practice FIELD, and inspection unless pre-approved by the Event Director or the Program Delivery Partner. Host teams supplying practice FIELD elements and/or machine shop resources may use them; however, teams registered for that event must be granted priority.

title: *Practice only when/where permitted
text:
*Practice only when/where permitted. Teams may only practice with their ROBOT in their pit space, in the designated event practice areas, or while in a Practice MATCH.

Teams may not set up their own practice equipment outside their pit in other areas of the event venue. If the Event Director determines a pit practice setup is unsafe or interferes with activity in adjacent pits or aisles, the team must discontinue the activity.

Demonstrating robot functionality to guests or JUDGES is not considered practice.

title: *Work in designated areas only
displayTitle: E108 Work in designated areas only
text:
*Work in designated areas only. At the event venue, teams may only produce FABRICATED ITEMS as follows:

A.      in their pit area,

B.      in another team’s pit area with permission from that team,

C.      while queued for a MATCH or practice FIELD (given space constraints, extra scrutiny regarding safety is required),

D.      any area designated by event staff (e.g., playoff pit area), or

E.      as permitted at provided machine shops that are available to all teams.

title: *Some things do not belong at events
displayTitle: E109 Some things do not belong at events
text:
*Some things do not belong at events. Do not bring or use the following:

A.      Skateboards,

B.      ‘hoverboards’,

C.      drones,

D.      bottled gas tanks (e.g., helium),

E.      noisy devices or noisemakers, such as floor stompers, whistles and/or air horns,

F.      walkie-talkies, or

G.     scooters, except for those used for accommodations.

title: *Do not arrange for additional utilities
displayTitle: E110 Do not arrange for additional utilities
text: *Do not arrange for additional utilities. Do not arrange for power, internet access, or phone lines from venue service providers or attempt to use venue internet connections reserved for event purposes (e.g., FIRST event management software or webcasting).

title: *Do not sell stuff
text: *Do not sell stuff. Teams may not conduct sales at an event. This includes, but is not limited to, raffle tickets, food, hats, shirts, candy, water, soft drinks, fruit, or any promotional products unless specifically allowed by the Event Director.

title: *Make FIRST loud, but with restrictions
displayTitle: E112 Make FIRST loud, but with restrictions
text: *Make FIRST loud, but with restrictions. Do not invite or bring live bands to play in the audience. Do not play loud music.

title: *Hang banners with care
text:
*Hang banners with care. Be respectful when hanging your banners.

A.      Do not cover or move other team or sponsor signs already in place.

B.      Share the available space fairly with other teams.

C.      Do not obstruct the view of spectators.

D.      Get permission from the Event Director before hanging banners outside of your pit.

E.      Hang signs and banners in a safe manner.

F.      Banners hung outside team pits must not be larger than 25 ft.2 (2.3 m2).

We encourage teams to bring team flags and/or signs for display in their pits and/or the ARENA.

Respect venue-specific rules regarding sign location and hanging methods. At the end of the event, safely remove all signs and anything used to hang the signs (tape, string, etc.).

title: *Limit flag and flagpole size if used in the ARENA
displayTitle: E114 Limit flag and flagpole size if used in the ARENA
text:
*Limit flag and flagpole size if used in the ARENA. Flags and flagpoles may not be of unreasonable size and weight if they are going to be used around the FIELD. 

As a guideline, reasonable flags are less than 3 ft. by 5 ft. (~91 cm by 152 cm) in size and weigh less than 2 lbs. (~907g). Reasonable flagpoles may not be more than 8 ft. (~243 cm) long and must weigh less than 3 lbs. (~1360g).

title: *No firearms or other weapons
displayTitle: E115 No firearms or other weapons
text: *No firearms or other weapons. Firearms or other weapons are prohibited at all FIRST events for all FIRST programs, including without limitation, all official FIRST Events posted here. This rule includes prop or simulated weapons which appear to be real. This policy does not apply to law enforcement or venue security personnel.

title: *Inspection required for practice FIELD access
displayTitle: E116 Inspection required for practice FIELD access
text: *Inspection required for practice FIELD access. A team may only use a practice FIELD with a ROBOT that has passed an initial, complete inspection. This rule only applies to events not using scheduled inspection times.

title: *Do not record anyone at the event without their consent
displayTitle: E117 Do not record anyone at the event without their consent
text:
*Do not record anyone at the event without their consent. Do not record interactions with anyone at an event, without the person’s consent. FIRST event staff and volunteers are empowered to excuse themselves from an interaction in which they are being recorded after declining consent.

Please note that many FIRST events are livestreamed and FIRST participants have given permission to appear in footage from FIRST. This does not mean that people can record specific interactions without additional consent.

Laws regarding recording of conversations vary state-to-state and country-to country, and, in some cases, recording without consent may be criminal. Introducing the idea of recording a conversation with an implied reason of proving someone’s error can escalate a discussion and is likely to increase its adversarial nature.

title: *Quiet in the pits during ceremonies
displayTitle: E701 Quiet in the pits during ceremonies
text:
*Quiet in the pits during ceremonies. During ceremonies outside of Playoff MATCHES, team members may not:

A.      use power tools

B.      use loud hand tools (hammers, saws, etc.), or

C.      shout, yell, or use loud voices, unless as a demonstration of approval during a ceremonial activity.

title: *Pit person limit during ceremonies is 5
displayTitle: E702 Pit person limit during ceremonies is 5
text:
*Pit person limit during ceremonies is 5. No more than 5 team members may be in the pits during ceremonies outside of Playoff MATCHES. Each team must have at least 1 representative observing ceremonies to be responsible for relaying important information to the entire team.

All teams are encouraged to have as many people in the stands for ceremonies as possible. This is important both to celebrate all who are recognized during ceremonies, but also to listen for important day-of information from event organizers which might be critical for your team.

title: *Be respectful during anthems
text: *Be respectful during anthems. Team members, including any remaining in the pits, should exhibit peaceful behavior during the presentation of all national anthems. If team members wish to abstain from traditional anthem observance behaviors, they have a right to do so, as long as they remain silent and non-disruptive.

title: *No saving seats
text:
*No saving seats. Teams are not permitted to save or designate seats for team members that are not actively using them.

Teams may not hang banners or ribbons or otherwise designate seating. (Event staff will remove and discard any banners, roping, etc., used to designate seating.) Please take turns sitting in the bleachers/stands if seating is limited. If there is a crowding problem, we ask that you kindly leave after your team's MATCH and return later, if possible.

The Event Director may reserve seats for attendees who require accessible seating, for certain volunteers, or to ensure teams in the Playoffs have seats to watch their teams play.

title: *No throwing items from the stands
displayTitle: E802 No throwing items from the stands
text: *No throwing items from the stands. Items may not be thrown from the audience seating.

title: Team PORTFOLIOS have limits
text:
Teams have the opportunity to submit a team PORTFOLIO to be used as part of the judging process. No other printed or digital content not directly included in this document will be collected by the JUDGES to consider during deliberations. Team PORTFOLIOS must meet the following requirements:
A. must consist of 1 cover page including the team number and optionally: team name, PORTFOLIO table of contents, team organizations, sponsors, logo, motto, and picture of the ROBOT and/or team,
B. no more than 15 pages of content,
C. use only US Letter (8.5” x 11”) or A4 (210 x 297 mm) size pages,
D. if submitted digitally, the complete submission must be less than 15MB in size, and
E. must only include progress, challenges, and accomplishments which have taken place since January 1, 2025.
None of the content of the cover page will be used by JUDGES to evaluate any awards criteria. Any content beyond the allowed 15 pages will not be reviewed by the JUDGES.

title: PORTFOLIOS must be submitted on time and as requested
displayTitle: A202 PORTFOLIOS must be submitted on time and as requested
text:
Teams must submit their PORTFOLIO as instructed by the Event Director and by the stated deadline if they wish to have it considered during the judging process. If no other instructions are provided, teams should submit 1 printed copy of their PORTFOLIO during the structured interview.
Instructions about when and how teams should submit their PORTFOLIOS should be communicated by the Event Director before the event.
If circumstances prevent a team from following the PORTFOLIO submission instructions, the Event Director should work with the JUDGE Advisor to make reasonable accommodations to accept all team PORTFOLIOS unless doing so poses an undue burden to the judging process.

title: Teams must attend a structured interview session
displayTitle: A203 Teams must attend a structured interview session
text:
To be considered for any judged awards the team must attend their assigned structured interview session.
Teams should be informed of their assigned time by the Event Director or local Program Delivery Partner in advance of the event. If there is a schedule conflict or the team misses their structured interview slot due to unforeseen circumstances the team should work with the Event Director or local Program Delivery Partner to make reasonable alternate accommodations for a structured interview at the event if possible.

title: Bring the right resources with you for your structured interview
displayTitle: A204 Bring the right resources with you for your structured interview
text:
Teams attending their structured interview time slot should come prepared with the following:
A. no less than 2 STUDENT representatives for teams of 2 STUDENTS and larger,
B. a printed copy of their team PORTFOLIO (optional, submit as instructed by the Event Director),
C. “show and tell” demonstration items which may include the team’s ROBOT (encouraged, but optional),
D. 1 silent observer per A208 (optional), and
E. 1 support person to fill accommodation needs per A209 (optional, as needed).
Teams are encouraged to have as many STUDENTS as possible involved in the structured interview process.
A team does not have to have a ROBOT to participate in judging or be eligible for judged awards.
Teams may power on and demonstrate their ROBOT functions during the structured interview unless explicitly disallowed by the Event Director or Local Program Delivery Partner. All teams should have the same demonstration restrictions.

title: Everyone gets equal structured interview time
displayTitle: A205 Everyone gets equal structured interview time
text: All teams will be scheduled for the same length structured interview of at least 10 minutes with a minimum of 10 minutes reserved between structured interviews for JUDGES to confer.

title: The structured interview timer starts when the team starts
displayTitle: A206 The structured interview timer starts when the team starts
text:
The timer starts after the team has entered the room and when they begin their presentation. Teams who take an extended amount of time to begin will be warned by the JUDGES to begin promptly and then the structured interview timer will be started regardless of the readiness of the presenting team.
Teams should enter the room and prepare to begin speaking in an expedited manner. Do not attempt to abuse the delayed start timer to set up equipment or otherwise gain an advantage.

title: Prepared structured presentation time should not be interrupted
displayTitle: A207 Prepared structured presentation time should not be interrupted
text: The first 5 minutes of the structured interview are reserved for the team to present a prepared oral presentation uninterrupted, if they choose. The uninterrupted presentation time may be ended early by the team. Any remaining time should be a question and answer conversation with the STUDENTS and led by the JUDGES.

title: One adult silent observer is welcome
displayTitle: A208 One adult silent observer is welcome
text: One adult mentor may attend the judging session and be present for any interaction between the JUDGES and the STUDENT team members. The adult observer and mentor(s) may not interact or actively coach during any interaction between the JUDGES and the STUDENT team members.

title: Translator and/or Sign Language Interpreter accommodations
displayTitle: A209 Translator and/or Sign Language Interpreter accommodations
text: Teams who need to use a translator to communicate with the JUDGES may provide one if the team’s native language does not match that of the event host site provided JUDGES. Teams who intend to interview with the assistance of a translator must work with the Event Director in advance to request additional interview time of between 2 and 5 minutes, if needed.

title: No Photos, Video or Audio recording during structured interview
displayTitle: A210 No Photos, Video or Audio recording during structured interview
text: In addition to the restrictions of E117, no recording of video or audio, or photos may be taken during the structured interview.

title: The number of awards given scales with event size
displayTitle: A211 The number of awards given scales with event size
text: The total number of awards given is based on the number of teams checked in at the event. Not all awards are given at every competition. Only the awards specified in Table 6-1 based on the event size are points-eligible for advancement.

title: Judging feedback is provided to all teams
displayTitle: A212 Judging feedback is provided to all teams
text: All teams will receive feedback from their structured interview session. The JUDGES complete a form immediately following the structured interview based on their initial impression of the team.

title: Teams are only eligible to win the Inspire Award in their own region
displayTitle: A213 Teams are only eligible to win the Inspire Award in their own region
text: Teams are only eligible to be considered for the Inspire Award (1st, 2nd or 3rd place) when competing at a tournament within their own region.

title: Teams cannot win the Inspire Award at multiple Qualifying or League Tournaments
displayTitle: A214 Teams cannot win the Inspire Award at multiple Qualifying or League Tournaments
text: Teams are only eligible to win 1st place Inspire Award once per season from any Qualifying or League Tournament. Teams who have won 1st Place Inspire are eligible to win 2nd or 3rd place Inspire Award at subsequent Qualifying or League Tournaments.

title: Teams can only get one judged award
displayTitle: A215 Teams can only get one judged award
text: Teams are only eligible to win or be a runner-up for a single judged award at the event.

title: Inspire Award
text:
The team that receives this award is a strong ambassador for FIRST programs and a role model FIRST team. This team is a top contender for many other judged awards and is a gracious competitor.
The Inspire Award winner is an inspiration to other teams, acting with Gracious Professionalism® both on and off the playing FIELD. This team shares their experiences, enthusiasm, and knowledge with other teams, sponsors, their community, and the JUDGES. Working as a unit, this team will have shown success in performing the task of designing and building a ROBOT.

title: Think Award
text: This judged award is given to the team that best reflects the journey the team took as they experienced their season. The content within the PORTFOLIO is the key reference for JUDGES to help identify the most deserving team.

title: Connect Award
text: This judged award is given to the team that connects with their local science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) community to learn and adopt new tools through effort and persistence. This team has a team plan and has identified steps to achieve their goals.

title: Reach Award
text: This award celebrates a team that has introduced and recruited new people into FIRST. Through their efforts, they have sparked others to embrace the FIRST culture.

title: Sustain Award
text: Sustainability and planning are essential for a FIRST team, because they ensure the program’s long-term success. This award celebrates the team that has considered their future team members and has worked to ensure that their team or program will continue to exist long after they have gone on to develop their careers.

title: Innovate Award sponsored by RTX
text: The Innovate Award celebrates a team that thinks imaginatively and has the ingenuity, creativity, and inventiveness to make their designs come to life. This judged award is given to the team that has an innovative and creative ROBOT design solution to any specific components in the FIRST Tech Challenge game.

title: Control Award
text: The Control Award celebrates a team that uses sensors and software to increase the ROBOT’S functionality during gameplay. This award is given to the team that demonstrates innovative thinking and solutions to solve game challenges such as autonomous operation, improving mechanical systems with intelligent control, or using sensors to achieve better results.

title: Design Award
text: The Design Award celebrates the team that demonstrates an understanding of industrial design principles by striking a balance between form, function, and aesthetics while meeting the needs of this season’s challenge.

title: Judges' Choice Award
text: During the competition, the judging panel may meet a team whose unique efforts, performance, or dynamics merit recognition, but does not fit into any of the other award categories.

title: Winning Alliance Award
text: This award will be given to the winning ALLIANCE represented in the final MATCH of the Playoffs of a single-division Tournament or Championship event.

title: Finalist Alliance Award
text: This award will be given to the finalist ALLIANCE represented in the final MATCH of the Playoffs of a single-division Tournament or Championship event.

title: FIRST Leadership Award
text: The STUDENTS who earn FIRST Leadership Award status as a semi-finalist, finalist or winner are great examples of current STUDENT leaders who have led their teams and communities to increased awareness for FIRST and its mission.

title: Compass Award
text: This award recognizes an adult coach or mentor who has given outstanding guidance and support to a team throughout the year and demonstrates Gracious Professionalism®.

title: Digital Animation Award sponsored by Worcester Polytechnic Institute
displayTitle: 6.6.1 Digital Animation Award sponsored by Worcester Polytechnic Institute
text: This award celebrates STEAM and emphasizes the ability to tell a story through animation that integrates technological, social, and humanistic concepts.

title: Safety Animation Award sponsored by UL Solutions
displayTitle: 6.6.2 Safety Animation Award sponsored by UL Solutions
text: The theme for the Safety Animation Award is Unearth Safety. Teams are invited to create an animation that promotes safe and sustainable practices and inspires responsible exploration and stewardship of resources.

title: Game Overview
text:
In DECODE™ presented by RTX 2 competing ALLIANCES of 2 teams each score purple and green ARTIFACTS in their GOAL, build PATTERNS, and race back to their BASE before time runs out.

Just before the match starts, the OBELISK is randomized to show one of 3 MOTIFS. The MOTIF for the MATCH defines what color PATTERN robots try to create on their RAMPS.

During the first 30 seconds of the MATCH, the ROBOTS operate autonomously. ROBOTS can use sensors to decode the randomized MATCH MOTIF. ROBOTS can earn points by scoring ARTIFACTS in their GOAL and building a PATTERN on their RAMP based on the MOTIF. ROBOTS also earn points for moving off the LAUNCH LINE.

During the remaining 2 minutes of the MATCH, human DRIVERS take control of their ROBOT. ROBOTS collect and continue to score ARTIFACTS in their GOAL to earn points. DRIVE TEAM members can retrieve ARTIFACTS from the ALLIANCE’S LOADING ZONE and help their ROBOTS by loading them with ARTIFACTS.

As time runs out, ALLIANCES can work together to return both of their ROBOTS to the BASE. ALLIANCES that build PATTERNS based on the MOTIF at the end of the MATCH earn additional points.

The ALLIANCE that earns the most points wins the MATCH and additional RANKING POINTS can be earned though completing other scoring achievements.

title: ARENA
text:
The ARENA includes all elements of the game infrastructure that are required to play DECODE: the FIELD, SCORING ELEMENTS, queue area, team media area, and all equipment needed for event management.

The ARENA is modular and is assembled, used, disassembled, and transported many times during the competition season. It undergoes wear and tear. The ARENA is designed to withstand rigorous play and frequent reassembly. Every effort is made to ensure that ARENAS are consistent from event to event.

However, ARENAS are assembled in different venues by different event staff and volunteers, and some small variations occur. Teams should design ROBOTS that are insensitive to these variations.

title: Dimensions and Accuracy
text:
The specifications for the DECODE FIELD can be retrieved from several official sources including the 3D CAD model, Competition Manual illustrations, FIELD Setup Guide, FIELD Acceptance Checklist, and FIELD Mitigation Guide.

The 3D CAD model is the official representation of the FIELD. Measurements may be taken with a general tolerance of +/- 1 in. (+/- 2.5 cm).

Illustrations in the manual are for visual understanding only and dimensions shown are nominal unless otherwise noted.

The ARENA is modular and subject to wear and variation between events. Teams should design ROBOTS that are insensitive to these variations.

title: FIELD
text:
Each FIELD is approximately 144 in. by 144 in. and is bounded by FIELD perimeter walls. The surface consists of 36 interlocking foam TILES approximately 24 in. by 24 in.

Each FIELD includes 1 CLASSIFIER per ALLIANCE, 1 GOAL per ALLIANCE, and 1 OBELISK.

Official FIELDs use AndyMark DECODE FIELD components or equivalent. The surface uses FIRST Tech Challenge Field Soft Tiles. The perimeter uses the FTC Perimeter Kit or equivalent.

Some events may raise the FIELD while ALLIANCE AREAS remain at ground level.

title: Areas, Zones, & Markings
text:
FIELD zones define spaces inside the FIELD, while areas define spaces outside the FIELD.

Tape is typically 1 in. gaffer tape in red, blue, and white.

Key areas and zones include the ALLIANCE AREA, DEPOT, LAUNCH LINE, and LAUNCH ZONES.

Additional zones include the BASE ZONE, GATE ZONE, LOADING ZONE, SECRET TUNNEL ZONE, and SPIKE MARKS.

REFEREES treat all tape lines as continuous even if gaps exist due to tile seams or installation methods.

title: TILE Coordinates
text: TILE coordinates are used to assist with FIELD setup. The coordinate system defines intersections of TILE tabs and provides a grid reference system for FIELD elements.

title: ALLIANCE AREA
text:
The ALLIANCE AREA is the designated red or blue space adjacent to the FIELD where DRIVE TEAMS stage during a MATCH.

Operator consoles are placed on provided tables when available and may not be moved without permission from FIELD STAFF.

The FIELD is oriented so the red ALLIANCE AREA is on the left from the primary audience perspective.

title: OBELISK
text:
The OBELISK is a triangular prism located outside the FIELD near the GOAL side.

It is approximately 23 in. tall with rectangular faces approximately 11 in. wide.

Each face contains an AprilTag corresponding to one of three MOTIFS: GPP, PGP, or PPG.

The OBELISK is randomly oriented each MATCH by FIELD STAFF. Its position is not intended for navigation or deterministic field reference.

title: GOAL
text:
The GOAL is a 3-sided structure approximately 27 in. by 27 in. and 54 in. tall.

It is made primarily of corrugated polypropylene sheet material.

The GOAL includes a top opening for scoring and an archway exit connected to the CLASSIFIER.

The top lip is approximately 38.75 in. above the TILE surface.

title: CLASSIFIER
text:
The CLASSIFIER is attached to the GOAL and includes three main components: the SQUARE, RAMP, and GATE.

It is used to control how ARTIFACTS are scored and transferred within the GOAL system.

title: SQUARE
text: The SQUARE is located at the top of the RAMP and is the location where ARTIFACT scoring is evaluated.

title: RAMP
text:
The RAMP is an aluminum structure that can hold up to 9 CLASSIFIED ARTIFACTS before overflow occurs.

In some cases, high-speed or spinning ARTIFACTS may bypass available slots and overflow. This is considered normal FIELD behavior and not a FIELD fault.

title: GATE
text:
The GATE is a robot-activated mechanism that releases ARTIFACTS from the RAMP.

It is gravity-closed and may open or close at variable speeds.

The GATE is not considered faulty if it closes inconsistently or takes time to reset.

Robots are expected to interact reliably with the GATE within a contact range of approximately 3 in. to 5.5 in. above the TILE surface.

title: SCORING ELEMENTS
text:
SCORING ELEMENTS are ARTIFACTS used in DECODE MATCHES.

ARTIFACTS are 5 in. nominal balls in purple and green colors.

There are 24 purple ARTIFACTS and 12 green ARTIFACTS per MATCH.

Actual size may vary slightly due to manufacturing tolerances.

title: AprilTags
text:
AprilTags are 8.125 in. square fiducial markers used for navigation and identification.

GOAL tags identify alliances: red uses ID 24 and blue uses ID 20.

OBELISK tags (IDs 21, 22, 23) correspond to MOTIFS.

OBELISK tags are not recommended for precise navigation due to variable placement.

title: FIELD STAFF
text:
FIELD STAFF are trained volunteers responsible for running MATCHES safely, fairly, and efficiently.

Key roles include:
- Head REFEREE: final authority on scoring and penalties
- FIRST Technical Advisor (FTA): ensures technical and field compliance
- FIELD Supervisor: manages match flow and field reset operations

title: Event Management System
text:
The Event Management System is the software and hardware system used to manage MATCH scoring, timing, and communications.

Audio cues are used as reference points during MATCHES, including:
- MATCH start: "Cavalry Charge"
- AUTO end: "Buzzer x3"
- TELEOP start: "3 Bells"
- Final 20 seconds: "Train Whistle"
- MATCH end: "3-second Buzzer"
- MATCH stopped: "Foghorn"

Visual timers are the official source if discrepancies occur.

title: Game Details
text:
In DECODE, 2 ALLIANCES (each consisting of 2 FIRST Tech Challenge teams) compete in MATCHES by scoring ARTIFACTS, building PATTERNS, and returning to BASE before time expires.

MATCHES include autonomous and driver-controlled periods, where ROBOTS collect and score ARTIFACTS into GOALS and RAMP systems based on a randomized MOTIF.

The MATCH winner is the ALLIANCE with the most points, with additional RANKING POINTS awarded for specific achievements.

title: MATCH Overview
text:
MATCHES run on a 5- to 12-minute cycle including setup, a 30-second AUTO period, an 8-second transition, a 2-minute TELEOP period, and post-MATCH reset.

During MATCHES, ROBOTS collect ARTIFACTS and score them into the GOAL to create PATTERNS based on the MOTIF. ARTIFACTS that do not drop into the RAMP are OVERFLOW. ROBOTS end MATCHES by returning to BASE.

title: DRIVE TEAM
text:
A DRIVE TEAM consists of up to 4 members from the same team responsible for MATCH performance. Roles include DRIVE COACH, DRIVER, and HUMAN PLAYER. Only 1 non-STUDENT is allowed per DRIVE TEAM.

DRIVE TEAMS are expected to consist of members present at the event, with limited flexibility for exceptional circumstances such as emergencies or delays.

Table 10-1 roles:
- DRIVE COACH: advisor (max 1)
- DRIVER: operator (up to 3 STUDENTS)
- HUMAN PLAYER: manages SCORING ELEMENTS

A STUDENT is anyone who has not completed secondary school as of Sept 1 of the season.

title: Setup
text:
Before each MATCH, FIELD STAFF stage SCORING ELEMENTS and DRIVE TEAMS stage ROBOTS and OPERATOR CONSOLES before taking positions.

DRIVE TEAMS must ensure proper staging conditions including correct personnel, badges, and readiness before MATCH start.

title: SCORING ELEMENTS
text:
24 purple and 12 green ARTIFACTS are staged across SPIKE MARKS, LOADING ZONES, and ALLIANCE AREAS in defined patterns.

Up to 3 ARTIFACTS may be pre-loaded onto ROBOTS. Placement follows fixed MOTIF-based staging rules.

title: DRIVE TEAMS Setup
text:
DRIVE TEAMS stage in their ALLIANCE AREA after the previous MATCH ends. Requirements include correct team members, valid inspection status, proper badge display, and correct positioning within their ALLIANCE AREA.

Failure to comply may result in rule violations.

title: OPERATOR CONSOLES
text:
DRIVE TEAMS configure OPERATOR CONSOLES before MATCH start. Teams select AUTO or TELEOP OpModes and initialize via the DRIVER STATION app using the INIT button.

Improper setup may delay MATCH readiness.

title: ROBOTS Setup
text:
ROBOTS are staged according to G304 rules. Placement order may alternate between ALLIANCES as directed by REFEREES.

In Qualification MATCHES, Red/Blue 1 places first. In Playoffs, ALLIANCE CAPTAINS determine placement order.

title: MATCH Periods
text:
Each MATCH includes a 30-second AUTO period, an 8-second transition, and a 2-minute TELEOP period.

AUTO is fully autonomous. TELEOP is driver-controlled.

title: Scoring
text:
ALLIANCES score points by LEAVING LAUNCH LINE, scoring ARTIFACTS, achieving PATTERNS, scoring DEPOTS, and returning to BASE.

Points contribute to MATCH results and RANKING POINTS for standings.

title: ARTIFACT Scoring Criteria
text:
ARTIFACTS are classified as CLASSIFIED or OVERFLOW depending on their path through the GOAL, SQUARE, and RAMP.

CLASSIFIED ARTIFACTS go directly to the RAMP. OVERFLOW ARTIFACTS pass through but do not meet CLASSIFIED criteria.

DEPOT scoring occurs when ARTIFACTS are placed over the DEPOT zone regardless of ROBOT interaction.

title: PATTERN Scoring Criteria
text:
PATTERN scoring is based on matching ARTIFACT colors on the RAMP with the MOTIF defined by the OBELISK.

The MOTIF is repeated across 9 positions on the RAMP. Points are awarded for each correct match.

title: ROBOT Scoring Criteria
text:
LEAVE points are earned when a ROBOT leaves the LAUNCH LINE during AUTO.

BASE scoring depends on whether a ROBOT is partially or fully supported by the BASE ZONE TILE at MATCH end.

Full support = fully returned. Partial support = partially returned.

title: Point Values
text:
CLASSIFIED ARTIFACTS: 3 AUTO / 3 TELEOP
OVERFLOW ARTIFACTS: 1 AUTO / 1 TELEOP
DEPOT: 1 point
PATTERN match: 2 points per phase
BASE partial: 5 points
BASE full: 10 points
Bonus: 2 ROBOTS fully returned = 10 bonus RP

Ranking Points are awarded for MOVEMENT, GOAL, PATTERN, and MATCH results.

title: Violations
text:
Violations include MINOR FOUL (5 points), MAJOR FOUL (15 points), YELLOW CARD, RED CARD, DISABLED, DISQUALIFIED, VERBAL WARNING, and RP restrictions.

Multiple violations may apply simultaneously. REFEREES determine enforcement.

title: YELLOW and RED CARDS
text:
YELLOW CARDS are warnings for serious violations. Two YELLOW CARDS become a RED CARD.

CARDS persist through event phases unless cleared. RED CARDS result in MATCH DISQUALIFICATION.

title: CARD Application
text:
CARDS are applied based on when violations occur relative to Qualification and Playoff MATCHES.

Timing determines which MATCH the penalty applies to.

title: Playoff CARD Rules
text:
During Playoffs, CARDS apply to the entire ALLIANCE instead of individual teams.

Two YELLOW CARDS result in a RED CARD and MATCH DISQUALIFICATION.

title: Violation Examples
text:
Violation examples explain how MINOR FOULS, MAJOR FOULS, and CARDS are applied.

Penalties may escalate based on repetition, severity, or match conditions.

title: Head REFEREE
text:
The Head REFEREE has final authority on all MATCH decisions. No video or external review is used.

All rulings made on-field are final.

title: Other Logistics
text:
SCORING ELEMENTS leaving the FIELD are returned by FIELD STAFF.

ARENA FAULTS are not called for minor setup issues.

MATCH reset occurs between MATCHES with FIELD STAFF preparing the next round.

title: Personal Safety
text: G101 Humans, stay off the FIELD during the MATCH except for allowed setup and retrieval. VERBAL WARNING for violation. G102 prohibits climbing, hanging, manipulating, or damaging ARENA elements. VERBAL WARNING with escalation to YELLOW CARD for repeated violations.

title: Conduct
text: G201 requires civil and respectful behavior following FIRST Core Values. G202 prohibits interfering with opposing ALLIANCE. G203 prohibits encouraging teams to throw MATCHES. G204 prohibits accepting instructions to throw MATCHES. G205 prohibits intentional losing or ranking manipulation. G206 prohibits collusion affecting ranking points. G207 restricts misuse of ARENA access. Violations escalate from VERBAL WARNING to RED CARD.

title: Pre-MATCH Rules
text: G301 requires teams to be ready on time or risk FOULS, DISABLE, or MATCH penalties. G302 limits items brought to FIELD for safety and visibility. G303 requires robots to meet inspection and safety requirements before MATCH. G304 defines correct robot placement and starting configuration. G305 requires selecting and initializing OpMode before MATCH begins.

title: AUTO Rules
text: G401 restricts driver interaction during AUTO except start/stop safety actions. G402 prohibits interference with opponent robots or artifacts during AUTO. Violations result in MAJOR FOULS and possible ranking point loss.

title: Transition and TELEOP
text: G403 requires robots to remain motionless between AUTO and TELEOP. G404 requires robots to stop at end of TELEOP until released. Violations result in FOULS or RED CARDS depending on severity.

title: Scoring Elements
text: G405 prohibits misuse of scoring elements. G406 prohibits ejecting scoring elements from FIELD. G407 prohibits damaging scoring elements. G408 limits control to 3 artifacts. Violations range from MINOR FOUL to YELLOW CARD.

title: Robot Rules
text: G409 requires safe robot operation. G410 requires immediate compliance with disable commands. G411 requires visible identification. G412 prohibits field damage. G413 restricts entanglement and attachment. G414 and G415 define expansion limits. G416 restricts launching zones. G417–G419 regulate gate and ramp interactions. Violations escalate to RED CARD depending on severity.

title: Opponent Interaction
text: G420 prohibits deliberate damage or functional impairment of opponent robots. G421 prohibits tipping or entanglement. G422 limits pinning to 3 seconds. G423 prohibits blocking major gameplay areas. G424–G427 define protected zones including GATE ZONE, SECRET TUNNEL, LOADING ZONE, and BASE ZONE with varying penalties.

title: Human Rules
text: G428 requires DRIVE TEAM members to stay in ALLIANCE AREA. G429 restricts DRIVE COACH interaction with controls. G430 prohibits coach contact with scoring elements. G431 restricts human contact with robots or FIELD during MATCH. G432 limits artifact handling to LOADING ZONE rules. G433 restricts item placement on FIELD. G434 limits out-of-play artifact storage to 6 per alliance.

title: ROBOT Construction Rules
text: Section 12 defines how FTC ROBOTS must be built, including legal parts, materials, and construction limits. ROBOTS are electromechanical systems consisting of power, control, communication, and movement systems. Components are individual parts, while mechanisms are assemblies of components. Rules ensure safety, fairness, reliability, and consistent access to materials through defined COTS (Commercial-Off-The-Shelf) parts and vendors. Fabricated items are modified or built parts, while COTS items must remain unmodified. Vendors must be legitimate businesses, publicly available, and not exclusive to teams.

title: General ROBOT Design
text: R101 limits ROBOTS to an 18-inch cube starting configuration except for pre-loaded SCORING ELEMENTS. R102 requires ROBOTS to be self-supporting and allow powered or mechanical holding during inspection. R103 states there is no weight limit. R104 prohibits intentional detaching of parts. R105 defines post-start expansion limits: horizontal expansion is restricted to an 18x18 in. footprint, and vertical expansion is limited to 18 in., with up to 38 in. allowed under specific conditions.

title: ROBOT Safety & Damage Prevention
text: R201 prohibits traction systems that damage FIELD TILE. R202 bans sharp edges. R203 requires safe design and prohibits hazardous materials, weapons, interference devices, unsafe fluids, or entanglement risks. R204 ensures SCORING ELEMENTS can be removed safely. R205 prohibits messy or contaminating materials. R206 prevents SCORING ELEMENT damage. R207 restricts use of air systems and airflow devices. R208 prohibits suction or downforce systems that grip the floor.

title: Fabrication Rules
text: R301 restricts COTS MECHANISMS that are complete game solutions, with exceptions for drivetrains and Starterbots. R302 allows modification of legal COTS parts and raw materials. R303 requires COTS mechanisms to have only one degree of freedom with defined exceptions such as wheels, gearboxes, and joints. R304 and R305 allow reuse of prior year parts and software. R306 prohibits using SCORING ELEMENTS in robot construction. R307 allows offsite and after-hours work during events with safety expectations.

title: ROBOT SIGN Rules
text: R401 requires at least two durable ROBOT SIGNS placed on the robot for identification, sized at minimum 6.5 by 2.5 inches. R402 requires clear red or blue alliance color display with restrictions on additional markings. R403 requires visible team numbers using white opaque characters with size and spacing rules. ROBOT SIGNS must be durable, readable from distance, and not powered or illuminated. Temporary substitutions may be allowed if materials are unavailable at an event.

title: Robot Motors & Actuators Rules
text: R501 Allowable motors: Only approved 12V DC motors such as NeveRest, goBILDA, REV, TETRIX, and similar listed motors are allowed. R502 Allowable servos: Servos must meet strict electrical limits including stall current and power output restrictions. R503 Motor/servo limits: A robot may use at most 8 motors and 10 servos total. R504 Motor modification rules: Motors and servos cannot be modified except for mounting, wiring adjustments, labeling, insulation, repairs, or manufacturer-approved changes. R505 Power regulation: All actuators must be controlled through approved power regulation devices such as REV hubs or servo/motor controllers, each with strict port limits. R506 No relays or electromagnets: Relays, solenoids, electromagnets, and similar actuation systems are not allowed.

title: Robot Power & Electrical System Rules
text: R601 Battery limit: Only one approved 12V NiMH battery may power the robot. R602 Secondary batteries: Only small USB battery packs or camera batteries are allowed for peripherals and cannot power actuators or control systems. R603 Safe charging: Batteries must be charged using approved chargers and connectors only. R604 Charging limits: Charging must not exceed a 3-amp average current. R605 No ballast batteries: Extra batteries cannot be used for weight. R606 Battery mounting: Batteries must be securely mounted to survive impacts. R607 Electrical safety: All wiring must be insulated and use proper connectors. R608 Energy storage limits: Non-electrical energy must come only from gravity or elastic deformation. R609 Main power switch: All power must pass through a single approved main power switch. R610 Fuse rules: Fuses cannot be bypassed or upgraded beyond specification. R611 Frame grounding rules: The robot frame cannot carry electrical current except under strict grounding rules.

title: Robot Control, Software & Communication Rules
text: R701 Single robot controller: Robots must use one approved control system such as a REV Control Hub or Expansion Hub with smartphone. R702 No coprocessor modification: Coprocessor software cannot be modified unless explicitly allowed. R703 Vision systems: Only approved programmable vision systems are allowed. R704 Approved phones only: Only listed Android phones may be used as robot controllers. R705 USB connection rules: Smartphones must connect via USB OTG to the control hub. R706 Bandwidth limits: No continuous video streaming over Wi-Fi is allowed. R707 Device naming: Devices must follow team naming rules like 12345-RC and 12345-DS. R708 No interference: Only robot controller and driver station may communicate during matches. R709 No extra wireless: No additional wireless communication devices are allowed.

title: Pneumatics Rules
text: R801 No pneumatics: Closed air systems are not allowed on FTC robots except where explicitly permitted elsewhere in the rules.

title: Operator Console Rules
text: R901 DRIVER STATION device restriction: Only one approved Android-based DRIVER STATION device may be used and powered on. Allowed devices include REV Driver Hub or approved Android phones per R704 using OTG and USB connections. Spare devices are allowed only if not powered on simultaneously. R902 Accessibility requirements: The DRIVER STATION touch screen must be accessible, visible, and fully usable without external devices like a mouse. R903 Gamepad limits: Only up to 2 electrically unmodified gamepads are allowed from a specific approved list including Logitech F310, Xbox 360 controller, PS4 DualShock, PS5 controller (wired only), REV controllers, and similar supported devices. No modified electronics allowed. R904 Physical limits: The OPERATOR CONSOLE must fit within a 3 ft x 1 ft 2 in x 2 ft volume and should not exceed 20 lbs without scrutiny. Spare USB hubs are allowed but only one may be connected. R905 Wireless restrictions: Only the official robot controller and driver station communication is allowed during a match. No Bluetooth or additional wireless devices are allowed. R906 Safety and fairness: OPERATOR CONSOLES must not be unsafe, distracting, or interfere with other teams. They are intended only for organizing driver station equipment and not for additional match advantages.

title: Overview
text: Each FIRST Tech Challenge competition is played in a head-to-head tournament format consisting of Qualification MATCHES and Playoff MATCHES. Qualification MATCHES allow teams to earn MATCH points and RANKING POINTS that determine seeding for Playoff MATCHES. Playoff MATCHES determine the winning ALLIANCE. These rules apply to all FTC event types described in Section 4 Advancement, with additional League Play rules in Section 14.

title: General Tournament Rules
text: T201 Head REFEREE authority: The Head REFEREE has final authority over all gameplay decisions and rulings, and no video, photo, or external review is permitted. Event staff and FIRST personnel cannot overrule REFEREE decisions. T202 Only REFEREES may DISABLE a ROBOT during a MATCH. T203 Event Director authority covers all non-gameplay decisions including safety, venue, eligibility, and conduct. T204 All competition FIELDS must be consistent in setup. T205 During calibration periods, robots may not drive under their own power but may power on, run OpModes, extend mechanisms, or be manually moved; launching SCORING ELEMENTS is not allowed. T206 Teams receive minimum breaks of 5 minutes between Qualification MATCHES and 8 minutes between Playoff MATCHES. T207 MATCHES are played in numerical order unless extenuating circumstances require changes.

title: MATCH Replays
text: T301 MATCH replays are only allowed in rare cases involving ARENA FAULTS or safety stoppages. ARENA FAULTS include broken FIELD elements affecting gameplay, FIELD movement beyond tolerance, widespread wireless interference, timer failure, or FIELD STAFF error. Robot failures (battery, code, mechanical issues) are not valid reasons. T302 Replays attempt to replicate original conditions as closely as possible, including keeping disabled robots disabled and using the same FIELD when feasible.

title: Question Box (MATCH Clarifications)
text: Each event has a Question Box where one STUDENT per team (plus one silent observer) may speak with the Head REFEREE about MATCH rulings. Technical issues are handled by the FTA. REFEREES do not track detailed foul history and rely on observed information. Questions must be factual and timely. T401 limits discussion to one STUDENT and one silent observer. T402 defines strict timing windows for MATCH questions depending on Qualification or Playoff stage. T403 requires respectful, rule-based questions.

title: Practice MATCHES
text: Practice MATCHES occur before Qualification MATCHES when scheduled. Teams are randomly assigned and may not change MATCH assignments. Each team typically receives equal Practice MATCHES unless scheduling requires adjustments. Practice MATCHES are not guaranteed at all events.

title: Filler Line
text: The Filler Line is used to fill empty Practice MATCH slots. Eligible teams must have passed inspection (may be waived), must bring their ROBOT, may not work on their ROBOT while in line, may occupy only one spot, and cannot be in both a queued MATCH and the Filler Line at the same time.

title: Qualification MATCHES
text: Qualification MATCHES are scheduled so each team plays approximately 5–6 MATCHES depending on event size. Each round consists of one MATCH per team. Only eligible and checked-in teams are included in the schedule.

title: Schedule
text: Qualification MATCH schedules are released shortly before Qualification MATCHES begin. Each team plays one MATCH per round. Schedules may be distributed physically, posted publicly, or provided digitally depending on the event.

title: MATCH Assignment
text: MATCH assignments are generated by event software using rules that prioritize minimum time between matches, minimizing repeat alliances and opponents, reducing surrogate usage, and balancing red/blue assignments. SURROGATE MATCHES do not affect ranking. Back-to-back MATCH breaks are enforced per T206.

title: Qualification Ranking
text: Teams earn RANKING POINTS (RP) based on MATCH performance. A team’s RANKING SCORE (RS) is the average RP excluding SURROGATE MATCHES. Rankings are ordered by RS, then average MATCH points minus fouls, average base points, average auto points, and finally random sort.

title: Disqualification Effect
text: During Qualification MATCHES, DISQUALIFICATION only applies to the disqualified team and does not affect their ALLIANCE partner.

title: Overview
text: Each FIRST Tech Challenge competition is played in a head-to-head tournament format. Each tournament may consist of Qualification MATCHES and Playoff MATCHES. Qualification MATCHES allow teams to earn MATCH points and RANKING POINTS which determine seeding and may qualify them for Playoffs. Playoff MATCHES determine the event winning ALLIANCE. These rules apply to all event types described in section 4 Advancement. Additional rules may apply to League Meets and League Tournaments as covered by section 14 League Play Tournaments.

title: General Tournament Rules
text:
T201 Head REFEREE authority: The Head REFEREE has final authority over gameplay decisions. No video, photos, or recordings will be reviewed. Event Directors and Program Delivery Partners may not overrule Head REFEREE decisions. All MATCHES must be observed by a certified Head REFEREE. Rules may rely on human judgment and are enforced in good faith.
T202 Robot DISABLED: Only REFEREES may DISABLE a ROBOT during a MATCH.
T203 Event Director authority: The Event Director has authority over non-gameplay decisions such as venue access, pit space, safety, registration, and conduct outside the FIELD.
T204 FIELD consistency: All competition FIELDS must be consistent in setup including elevation, monitors, perimeter, and TILE type.
T205 Calibration rules: During FIELD measurement time, ROBOTS may not drive. They may run OpModes, calibrate sensors, and be moved manually. Violation results in warning then YELLOW CARD.
T206 MATCH breaks: Teams have minimum breaks between MATCHES (5 minutes Qualification, 8 minutes Playoffs). No team timeouts exist.
T207 MATCH order: MATCHES are played in numerical order unless extenuating circumstances occur.

title: MATCH Replays
text: T301 Replays allowed only in extreme ARENA FAULT conditions such as FIELD damage, timer failure, or interference affecting outcome. Robot issues like battery or programming are not valid. T302 Replay conditions: Efforts are made to replicate MATCH conditions. Disabled robots remain disabled. Starting positions and preloads may change if needed.

title: Clarifications (Question Box)
text: Teams may send 1 STUDENT representative to the Question Box for MATCH questions. Only 1 student and optionally 1 silent observer may attend discussions with the Head REFEREE. Questions must be timely (T402) and factual (T403). REFEREES may not recall exact foul details and provide general guidance instead.

title: Practice MATCHES
text: Practice MATCHES occur before Qualification MATCHES when available. Schedules are randomly assigned and equal for teams. Filler Line teams fill empty spots if they meet requirements: inspected ROBOT, present DRIVE TEAM, no working on ROBOT in line, and only one queue spot per team.

title: Qualification Schedule
text: Qualification schedules are released shortly before MATCHES begin. Each team plays one MATCH per round. Events schedule 5–6 Qualification MATCHES per team depending on event size. Schedules are distributed physically or digitally.

title: MATCH Assignment
text: Teams are assigned ALLIANCE partners using event software prioritizing: minimum time between MATCHES, minimizing repeat partners, minimizing opponents, reducing SURROGATES, and balancing red/blue assignments. Surrogate MATCHES do not affect ranking. Back-to-back MATCHES include mandatory breaks per T206.

title: Qualification Ranking
text: Teams earn RANKING POINTS (RP) each MATCH. Ranking Score is the average RP excluding surrogate MATCHES. Rankings are determined by RS, then MATCH points minus fouls, base points, AUTO points, and random sorting if needed. DISQUALIFICATION results in 0 contribution.

title: Playoff MATCHES
text: Playoff MATCHES use selected ALLIANCES and follow a double elimination format. No RANKING POINTS are earned. A DISQUALIFICATION applies to the entire ALLIANCE. T701 Teams must send a STUDENT representative or they are ineligible. T702 Declined teams cannot be selected by teams they rejected. T703 No backup teams allowed. T704 Extra pit crew members allowed (up to 3 additional) at discretion. T705 If both ALLIANCES are DISQUALIFIED, outcome depends on timing or may be a tie.

title: Alliance Selection
text: Top ranked teams become ALLIANCE CAPTAINS. Each selects one partner. If a selection is declined, lower alliances are promoted. If an alliance is incomplete, matches may proceed unevenly or result in automatic wins for opponents.

title: Playoff Bracket
text: Playoff size depends on number of teams: 2 alliances (4–10 teams), 4 alliances (11–20), 6 alliances (21–40), 8 alliances (41–64). Double elimination bracket with upper and lower brackets. Teams are eliminated after 2 losses. Ties replay. Color assignments follow bracket rules. MATCH delays follow T206.

title: 2-Alliance Bracket
text: Two alliances play finals directly. Bracket includes upper/lower logic simplified to a finals series with scheduled timing and award breaks.

title: 4-Alliance Bracket
text: Four alliance double elimination bracket with structured rounds, scheduled breaks, award intervals, and finals MATCH sequence.

title: 6-Alliance Bracket
text: Six alliance bracket includes upper and lower progression rounds, multiple elimination paths, structured timing gaps, and award breaks between stages.

title: 8-Alliance Bracket
text: Eight alliance bracket expands double elimination structure with more rounds, structured progression through upper/lower brackets, timed breaks, and final MATCH sequencing with awards.

title: Dual Division Events
text: Large events may be split into two divisions running parallel tournaments. Winners of each division compete for the overall event winner. T801 Both divisions use same bracket size based on smaller division. T802 Awards are given at event level. T803 Award counts are based on total teams.

title: Dual Division Advancement Points
text: Playoff advancement points: 40 for winners, 20 for finalists, 10 for division finalists, 5 for 3rd place teams.

title: Dual Division Playoffs
text: Each division runs full playoffs independently. Winners reset records and play a final bracket to determine event champion.

title: League Play Overview
text: Not all regions offer League Play. Leagues are closed groups of teams that participate in multiple League Meet events spread over weeks or months. Teams in a League should play a roughly equal number of MATCHES, with a minimum of 10 League Meet MATCHES per team. League Meet events consist of 5–6 Qualification MATCHES per team (as described in section 13.6 Qualification MATCHES) and do not include Playoff MATCHES or judging for awards. YELLOW and RED CARDS, VERBAL WARNINGS, and CARD penalties clear at the end of each League Meet event (see section 10.6.1). Teams may belong to only one League per season and may participate in only one League Tournament per season. Teams may only advance to a Regional Championship outside their region if approved by both Program Delivery Partners. League Tournaments function like Qualifying Tournaments including judging and advancement, except qualification rankings used for ALLIANCE selection and Qualification Round Performance Points include each team’s top 10 League Meet MATCHES plus League Tournament MATCHES. Top MATCHES are determined using the ranking sort order in Table 13-1. Teams with fewer than 10 League Meet MATCHES are assigned 0 for missing MATCHES in all scoring metrics. League Tournament advancement is based only on League Tournament performance except Qualification Round Performance, which includes League Meet results.

title: FIRST Championship Overview
text: At the 2025–26 FIRST Championship, teams are split into 6 divisions. Each division plays a standard tournament as described in section 13.6 Qualification MATCHES and section 13.7 Playoff MATCHES to produce Division Winning ALLIANCES. These 6 Division Winning ALLIANCES advance to Championship Playoffs to determine the FTC Championship Winners per section 15.5. Awards modifications: At Championship, judging is adjusted due to scale. Most awards are given per division, except Inspire Award (1st overall), FIRST Leadership Award (10 total), and Compass Award (1 total). Inspire Award winners are selected from division winners. Championship PORTFOLIO submission is required online between March 27 and April 6 (11:59 PM CDT). Championship interviews are pit-based, up to 10 minutes, including a 5-minute presentation option and standard questions; judging continues via portfolio and additional interviews. Compass Award videos are submitted by coaches by April 8. Game modifications: FIELD risers elevate fields ~24 inches, with aesthetic changes such as black anodized metal, matte AprilTags, partial OBELISK obstruction, rivets, and signage. AUTO to TELEOP transition is 15 seconds instead of 8. Championship uses 3-ROBOT ALLIANCES selected via extended draft (8 alliances, second selection round reversed order). Alliances may choose any 2 of 3 robots per match. Each division runs an 8-ALLIANCE double elimination playoff bracket per section 13.7.6. Pit crews may include up to 3 additional members. The 6 division winners then compete in a round-robin da Vinci tournament where each alliance plays all others once. Championship Points replace Ranking Points (2 for win, 1 tie, 0 loss). Rankings use Championship Score plus tie-breakers. Top 2 alliances advance to finals; first to 2 wins becomes champion. Tie matches are replayed until resolved.

title: Awards Modifications
text: Judging is modified at Championship due to scale. Most awards are given within each division only, except Inspire Award (overall 1st place selected from division winners), FIRST Leadership Award (10 total across event), and Compass Award (1 total). All teams are eligible for judged awards regardless of prior wins.

title: Championship Portfolio Submissions
text: Teams must submit PORTFOLIOS online before the event as part of judging. Submission window is March 27 to April 6 at 11:59 PM CDT. Submission issues are handled via customerservice@firstinspires.org. PORTFOLIOS are used in judging alongside interviews and other materials.

title: Championship Interview Process
text: Championship judging uses pit-based interviews instead of structured interviews. Each team receives up to 10 minutes with judges, including an optional 5-minute presentation. Standard questions include design compromises and team strategy. Additional questions may cover engineering and team attributes. Teams must attend the initial interview to be eligible for awards. Judges may continue evaluation using portfolios and additional pit interviews. Teams should be available in pits during judging windows.

title: Compass Award Submissions
text: Compass Award videos must be submitted by Lead Coach 1 or 2 by April 8 using the official submission form.

title: Game Modifications
text: Championship modifies field setup and timing. Fields are elevated approximately 24 inches. Changes are aesthetic and do not affect gameplay mechanics.

title: Fields
text: Championship fields are elevated on risers. Field staff and drivers remain at floor level. Some practice fields are also elevated. Aesthetic changes include black anodized metal parts, matte AprilTags, partial OBELISK obstruction (non-reliable side tags), aluminum rivets replacing some fasteners, and decorative signage on field walls.

title: Scoring and Timing
text: At Championship, the AUTO-to-TELEOP transition is 15 seconds instead of 8 seconds as defined in standard rules.

title: 3-Robot Alliances
text: Championship alliances consist of 3 robots instead of 2. Alliance selection follows standard process with an additional reversed second selection round to form 8 alliances of 3 robots each. In matches, alliances may choose any 2 of their 3 robots to compete. Decisions must not delay match start. In replay situations, the same robots must be used unless a robot is inoperable due to arena fault. This structure provides strategic flexibility and backup capability.

title: Championship Pit Crews
text: Each alliance may include up to 3 additional pit crew members inside the arena to assist with robot preparation and maintenance. These members may be students or adults, must remain in pit areas, and cannot participate in match play.

title: Championship Playoffs
text: Each division runs an 8-ALLIANCE double elimination playoff bracket per section 13.7.6. Division winners advance to championship finals. These 6 division winners compete in the da Vinci round-robin tournament to determine finalists and champion.

title: da Vinci Tournament MATCH Bracket
text: The 6 division champions compete in a round-robin format where each alliance plays every other alliance once. Matches are scheduled across multiple rounds with breaks. Match order is predefined and includes named division alliances.

title: da Vinci Round-Robin Ranking
text: Alliances earn Championship Points instead of Ranking Points: 2 for win, 1 for tie, 0 for loss. Disqualifications result in 0 points for the match. Championship Score is total points divided by matches played. Rankings are determined by Championship Score, then adjusted using match points minus fouls, base points, auto points, and random tiebreaking.

title: da Vinci Finals
text: The top 2 ranked alliances from round-robin advance to finals. Rank 1 is red alliance and rank 2 is blue alliance. The first alliance to win 2 matches becomes champion. If a match ends in a tie, an additional match is played until a winner is determined.
